The Rank 1 Frontline Guide to Stop Losing Games!
By Dishsoap • Published 6 days ago

Instaread

This guide teaches you how to flex any 4-Cost frontline based on what you hit from your level 8 rolldown. Being able to flex your frontline in this set is one of the reasons why I like it a lot more compared to previous sets. In Set 17, the Corki/Riven comp is very straightforward; there are no other variations, and you'd play the same comp every game.

Corki Riven Board Set 17

A similar example from this set is Aphelios Vanguards. However, the trait webs in this set allow more flexibility. None of the 4-Cost carries in this set require investment into their traits, and they can still be strong even with just trait activation. Aphelios only needs 2 Lunar and 2 Rapidfire to function, and there is no need to invest more into those traits, but investing into more frontline units instead is the way to go, and it doesn't have to be a 4 Vanguard frontline. In this comp, you can drop Taric and Hecarim for one other tank package like Sett and Gnar, or Amumu and Maokai.

Vanguards Aphelios Board
Brawlers Aphelios
Juggernauts Aphelios

The main 4-Cost tanks this set are Malphite, Sett, Sentinel, Amumu, and Lillia. All of them except Lillia can be the frontline unit of any board.

Malphite:

In the current meta, I Don't recommend flexing around Malphite, as he is the main tank of the most popular comps and is highly contested.

Malphite AP Flex
Malphite Sivir

In the Sivir comp, you can flex your frontline and replace Malphite and Rek'Sai with Sett. You can get 2 Extra team slots, as you are not sacrificing a unit from your board, and then you can flex any unit such as Ashe, Ivern, or Taric. But generally, playing Malphite REQUIRES activating Blackthorn; it gives Malphite useful stats that allow him to solo frontline.

Sett:

Sett is considered one of the most flexible tanks in this set, and he can be played in the Ahri board, Aphelios, Primals, Zyra, and even Ezreal. Sett only needs 2 Brawlers and a Warmong's to activate him.

Blossom Ahri
Ashe Fast 9
Aphelios Flex

Sentinel:

Almost all boards in this set have Sentinel in them, either as the main tank or a flex unit; his traits and kit are very useful and activate carries. Vanguards are the best tanking trait, especially at 4 Vanguards, and they can be the frontline of almost any comp.

Elderdragon Fast 9
Riftbeasts
Ahri Morgana
Aphelios Flex
Primal Sivir

Amumu:

Amumu this patch is really good after he got buffed; he is a bit less tanky compared to Sett but similar to Sentinel. Amumu can be flexed in the new 5 Rapidfire Aphelios board, and he can go into any Riftbeast flex board alongside Scuttlecrab; this goes into the Nidalee Sivir board and Alune Fast 9 setups. 4 and 6 Juggernaut boards are insane, and his Inferno trait is also useful, as it makes his stun last longer. He is also seen in the Malphite AP boards as a secondary tank or sacrificed for Blackthorn bonuses, and he can be primarily main-tanked on 2-Star with Lillia compared to Malphite 1-Star.

5 Rapidfire
Primal Flex
AP Fast 9
5 Cost Flex

Lilia:

The Main reason why Lillia isn't optimal as a main tank is that her Defender trait is the weakest tanking trait in this set, and Fae is hard to play around. Her Kit is also not the best, as she is considered a CC tank and is best positioned on the right or left side of the front row, which makes it easy for backline access. She can be seen in the Aphelios Elderwood board or the Fae Tristana reroll comp.
